Review Title: There are alternatives, don't let hotel lock you into flying Westwind
Review Text:
As an earlier reviewer mentioned, one of the Westwind planes (not the "Executive") has a "bench" at the back- with only a waist belt and no padding- which I was unfortunately assigned to (when the pilot planned the seating for weight distribution, as is always done, but could have been differently., but I was the last to board). The top of the window was below my chin when sitting on that bench, it's much higher than the seats. I am 71 and have spine degeneration, so I'd phoned in advance specifically to confirm that the padded seats and window type shown on their website is what we'd all have (the bench is Not shown).

Instead, I was crouched over on a hard bench to see out of the scratched windows, and it was miserable. They now deny I called, and say they routinely put elders and even handicapped guests on the "bench." So, beware, they're either lying about this to me or they're regularly putting guests in that painful position, for hours.

They blamed the hotel concierge, and fabricated other excuses. The 3-hour flight was supposed to include, as Lindsay explained in person right before the flight, a glide down into the canyon, a memorable experience only a plane could provide. But we did not do it. The conditions were good. There is other misrepresentation in their website, for instance, the seats and the planes are no longer in that condition, but show a lot of wear.

My family is in aviation, and I had confidence in Josh, the young pilot, to fly but not in his decision on the seating, and no confidence in the manager, Brad, who bullied me for complaining and requesting a refund. I regret trusting Hilton's Boulders Resort to arrange the canyon flight using Westwind. They have given me a 50% refund, but still blame me for having the "wrong expectations", and my spine is still painful.

Review Title: Waiting, waiting, more waiting - not worth the money; will be asking for partial refund
Review Text: Our family of four did the Adventure Tour - GC West Rim w/Skywalk package through WestWind during spring break in April 2023. While one would expect the the Grand Canyon to be a finely-tuned, well-oiled tourist machine, it definitely is not. While Westwind did their part in getting us safely from Sedona to the Grand Canyon and back - and we loved our pilot Brandon - what they don't emphasize is it that they are are the mercy of the Grand Canyon vendors - in our case Papillon Helicopters and whoever runs the Skywalk. For this cost, some VIP treatment is expected, but there is none. The first stop at the Skywalk and Eagle Point was so crowded that, because of the time limit we had in order to make our 1 pm helicopter ride, we had to choose between eating lunch or standing in the 2-3 hour Skywalk line. Since we had kids, we opted to eat, and still had to wait about 20 min for a table for burgers and chicken sandwiches. Then hopped back on the bus, were told we had to skip the Guano Point stop to make it to our 1 pm helicopter ride. Upon arriving at the Papillon Helicopters terminal, we were told it would be about 45 more min, which they kept telling us. Eventually, we made it on the helicopter at 3 pm, 2 hours past our assigned time that we rushed back for, skipping Guano Point and the Skywalk. The reasoning for the delay was that it was cold and 7 of their 8 helicopters were down for the day because of overnight freezing. Who in their right mind allows a $10M aircraft to freeze overnight? Is there no protocol in place to provide shelter for the $10M helicopters during freezing temperatures? Who is accountable for this? None of these questions were really answered. Once we did get on the helicopter, it was about a 5-min ride to the pontoon boat ride, which was pretty cool, but nowhere in the package description did it say anything about a pontoon boat ride and I would have rather had a longer helicopter ride. When they dropped us off for the pontoon boat ride, the now two functioning helicopters were taking turns dropping groups off, however we still had to wait about 45 min to get picked up after the boat tour was over. Waiting and being stuck somewhere for a ride were the themes of the day. This package is not worth the money. Overall, the GC does not have the infrastructure or processes in place to handle any kind of overwhelming number of spring break or holiday tourists. My hindsight advice would be: figure out a lesser traveled time to visit to GC; arrange your own travel so you're not stuck somewhere at the mercy of someone else; skip the Skywalk - it's little, not worth the wait, and you can't even take your own photos; do more research than I did, especially if traveling with kids; bring your own food; if you really want to do a helicopter tour, do not use Papillon, try the place next door - Maverick's Helicopters. As of this post, I have not received any refunds, but will be calling on Monday morning.

Captain Carla interupped the voice tour multiple times to point out various additional points of initerest! Captain even checked on how I was doing mid flight which was so kind!

The first view of the Grand Canyon in the distance is awesome! As we flew around the Canyon, the pictures and videos do not do it justice of the awe you feel viewing it from above! I am so very thankful I was able to complete the tour and feel I was able to do it because of Captain Carla. The Carla Touch:)

We were transferred to BuckWild Hummer Tour for the ground portion. I will review them on their page as well. Tom was our driver, the hummer was exceptionally comfortable, we traveled with a total of 12 guests. The rows of seats are stepped so the view from each row was great, not effected at all by persons in front of you! Great set up. Tom our driver was professional, and extremely knowledgable of all things related to The Grand Canyon park. It was a pleasure to get to know him during our 3 hour tour. He obviously loves his job and shares that feeling with his guests!

Our return flight to Sedona was a not as calm as outgoing but Captain Carla tried to find some smoother air but it was impossible. Even with the slight occassional bumps the flight was awesome, the views are just indescribable!

Thank you to Lindsey for arranging our reservation with kindness, and professionalism. Thank you to Captain Carla, without her calming, professionalism and expertise I don't know if I could have done it. Thank you to Tom for sharing his knowledge with us and his insights to The Grand Canyon as well as his wife who arranged all the lunches for our gourp!

Even got to do a little shopping in Hopi House, a high quality artsy Native American shop. And we saw a large elk cow browsing along the roadside!
The return flight was again narrated via our headsets, with more cool info, or we could talk to our fellow passengers with whom we had just spent the afternoon.
We returned to pick up a nice souvenir picture of myself and my husband, taken before departure.
I highly recommend this trip. We were staying in Scottsdale, and it was a short drive to the Deer Valley Airport. And off we flew with a guided tour via headsets from Phoenix to the West rim of the Grand Canyon. Once we arrived at the Grand Canyon airport we were immediately escorted over to of the helicopters. Again, no wait, quick effecient we were off in a helicopter escorting us down to The Colorado River Pontoon Boat excusion. Off the heli, now we hop on a boat. Id say we waited a total of 1 minute?
We were then greeted by our pontoon boat captain who drove us on a little tour down the river, with insight and information about the wonderous Canyon. Terrible that I cannot remember his name, I think Leo. Super friendly and took pictures of everyone on the boat.
After our boat ride we ran backup to the helicopter and requested once again to sit front row with the pilot.. Permission granted! This was the most well organized planned out thoughtful accommodating service oriented company and trip Ive done to date. You can not imagine, that in 7 hours, one could do all of this and be back for dinner! Take off at 11 am, back by 615
I am looking for an opportunity to come back out to Arizona again and would hands down absolutely do this day again!

Review Title: Bucket list but don't kick the bucket here
Review Text: The Skywalk is an engineering feat well documented in ASCE's Civil engineering magazine when it was built. But seeing it and standing on it is another experience. Just go there and enjoy the view because you can't take any pictures of yourself on the Skywalk - they do it for you at a price. Just as any other tourist trap, you could spend $80 on pictures only you can enjoy. The Skywalk is located at Eagle Point, which is an unprotected edge of the canyon. Don't be tempted to take a picture at the edge of a 4,000 feet drop. People die here trying to take pictures with their $2,000 Nikon. Be careful, stay off the edge. The only way to see all the attractions at Grand Canyon West is to park at the Airport and take a bus route run by the Havasupai Tribe. Buy the Legacy Gold ticket ($79.00) and you can visit three attractions - Skywalk, Eagle point (right there) and Guano Point  and get a lunch included. Just keep off the edge and enjoy the view. The bus route runs only in one direction so you cannot go back and forth. You can also catch a helicopter ride to the bottom of the canyon from the airport for $130 pp. The gift shop has some of the tribal handicrafts and all the other souvenirs and T-shirts made in China, all priced to help you remember the quality soon after you bought it. Having said all that - this is a must do trip, the views are exhilarating, the drive from Kingman is beautiful and if you pick a nice Spring day, you will love it and remember it for a life time.

Review Title: Understand What You Are Getting With The $700 Grand Canyon Plane, Helicopter and Boat Tour
Review Text:
This is not a direct slam against Westwind Air Service but rather a realistic view of the tour they offer and the control they do not have. Westwind flies you to the west rim Hualapai reservation and back, they book a helicopter ride through one of the services there and book the boat ride through a business owned by the Hualapai. There is a bus service that runs to 3 stops; a western town mock-up that we were not allowed to get off at, the sky-bridge area and an area we refer to as Guano Point where you get a lunch.
We paid $2800 for the four of us which we thought it was going to be an amazing first class adventure but unfortunately it turned out to be the equivalent of herding cattle.
We were most excited about the helicopter and boat ride but these turned out to be the worst part. We were told by Westwind that we would be the only ones in the helicopter which has 2 nice view seats in front and 4 very small seats across the back. When we got there, they crammed all of us into the back seats which were so tight that we could not even take pictures. When we got into the small tour boat it had engine and steering problems. By the time we got going the driver only went a couple of minutes up the river then turned off the engine. She was beyond rude when questioned about what was going on and kept sniping at people when they moved around to try and get better pictures. On top of that, this area was less than inspiring and did not make for good pictures which is not what we expected.
After the so-called boat ride we sat and waited, and waited, and waited for the unpleasant helicopter ride back. This significant delay compressed our time frame for everything else.
We next went to the Skywalk which is all about selling you the professional pictures since they do no allow you to take any. We could not appreciate the Skywalk because it was crazy busy and packed with people which was compounded by the photographers holding everybody back whenever they took pictures. The best pictures there are off to the side with the Skywalk in the background.
Next we were hustled off to Guano Point where we got a little cafeteria lunch. Guano Point is the best place to take photos as it extends well into the canyon and has great vistas on either side. We were enjoying exploring a little of this area when the pilot came up behind us and said it was time to go.
SUMMARY:
1. The plane ride is hot, loud, the tour information in the headphones is pretty much worthless and the person in the very back seat is only comfortable if you are a munchkin.
2. We did not receive the helicopter ride we were promised and it totally failed expectations - would not do again.
3. The boat ride was a joke with less than impressive vistas - would not do again.
4. The Skywalk was insanely busy and is not the best viewpoint - would not do again.
5. Guano Point was the best place for photos but we were not allowed enough time to appreciate it.
6. We did not see any "shows" as stated in the advertisement.
All in all we were expecting awe and grandeur but what we got was a crush of humanity in a get 'em in/get 'em out environment.
Like many things, being convenient to get to does not make it the best place to go.

Review Text:
This trip was amazing start to finish. Upon arrival at the airport we were greeted and given an overview of our day by a vibrant and friendly staff member. We were given free snacks (choices of Rice Krispie treats, pop tarts, granola bars, peanuts, trail mix, crackers etc.)and water to pack and take with us for the day. Got our pic taken in front of the plane and 5x7 prints given to us when we got back (ours came out a little blurry so you may wanna take some on your cell or personal camera too just in case). Bill our pilot was exceptional. He was friendly and informative and guided us throughout the day. The flight from Phoenix to the Grand Canyon was smooth and the plane was roomy. We had one stop in Sedona to pick up another family joining us on our tour and getting to see the red rocks of Sedona was an unexpected treat...the air strip was on top of a rock/mountain so quite the experience landing and taking off. Upon arrival at the canyon we went to the helicopter ride first. Exhilarating! First time on a helicopter and it was great. Ride was short to the base of the canyon then we got on a boat to ride in the Colorado for a bit. Our boat driver Jared was GREAT. He took the best pics of our group and did a 360 with the boat to get killer panoramic pics. After the boat ride it was back to the helicopter for another short ride back to the top of the canyon. From there we went to the Skywalk via a bus ride. Got suckered into buying all the pics since you can’t take your own camera but the pics are great—got all 14 on a jump drive for around 68 dollars. They do have lockers to put your stuff in free of charge since you can’t take them with you on the attraction. The skywalk was great but not as big as we expected. There is also a great ledge out front when you get off the bus to get some good pics. From there off to lunch...only disappointing part of trip. Was cafeteria type lunch with choice of meat, corn on cob that was dry and instant mashed potatoes with gravy. Salad, roll, and cookie included. Personally I would rather pack a lunch but it was included so really can’t complain. After lunch you can climb on the rock formations or hike for a bit at Guana point. Cool opportunity to take pics where it looks like you are hanging off the cliff. From there back to the bus and then the flight home. Left around 7:15 am and back around 2:45 pm....again had the extra stop in Sedona to drop off the other family. Got our pics given to us from the AM upon arrival and had a fresh brownie that was in the lobby while we waited for our Uber ride back to hotel. Overall great experience and I highly recommend.

Tips—
1. Bring a small bag that fits on your shoulder to carry water/snacks—we did small drawstring ones and it was perfect.
2. Load up on a few snacks and water provided upon arrival at Westwind so you don’t have to pay for them while at the canyon
3. Check weather. Parts of tour were cold so a light jacket was perfect.
4. Wear tennis shoes. Terrain is rocky/gravel and we saw way too many people in sandals or heels.
5. Wear sunscreen...especially on face, bring a hat if you like.
6. Sunglasses are a must.

Review Title: Flight from Hell over the Grand Canyon...
Review Text:
I'm conflicted as to how to review Westwind as we had two different planes for our group of 16 family and friends (ages ranging from 25 - 60) who had completely different experiences on our flight over the Grand Canyon from Page Airport. My flight (which I'll refer to as plane 1), which was supposedly the NON-executive plane, had an awesome pilot named Mark, who communicated with us throughout the flight, pointing out where to look (and there's a lot you won't see/notice if you're not directed) and forewarning us of turbulence. His humor and constant, clear communication made a semi-scary extremely turbulent flight as comfortable as it could possibly be. A few of us threw up from the bumpiness, but we felt very safe in Mark's hands and were all happy with our experience.

Our other plane of 8 people however (plane 2), had an entirely different experience. This plane we were told was the "executive plane" - nicer seats, etc. However, unlike plane 1 which had secure shoulder straps and individual seats for each person, this plane only had waist belts, the last row of the plane was a bench, and their seats were not in a fixed position and so were aggressively sliding back and forth throughout the flight. This constant movement, paired with turbulence, resulted in everyone slamming their heads into the ceiling multiple times (confirmed by every passenger) and 5 of the 8 passengers vomiting throughout the flight (so much vomit that my mom (the guest of honor) had to clean out the plane after they landed while the pilot stood by watching). One person got so sick they had to go to the hospital afterwards and 3 others were ill for the rest of the day and unable to participate in the activities we had planned. Of the 8 people on plane 2, only TWO people actually saw the Grand Canyon because the others were so sick, or scared that they couldn't look.

To make matters worse, their captain, unlike ours, did not speak once throughout the entire flight. Not only did this mean they weren't getting told where to look (which you think would be a no-brainer for a tour like this), but it also made everyone incredibly nervous as they continued to hit worse and worse turbulence. Honestly, when I initially heard how terrible a time they had, I thought they were being dramatic, but when I heard THESE details (seats sliding around, heads slamming into the ceiling, and a captain who did not speak the entire 1.5 hour flight) and they were confirmed by every single passenger, I was furious.

Upon landing, as the majority of our group was throwing up outside the airport, the captains told us that that was the worst conditions they've ever flown through and that they were cancelling the rest of the flights for that day. While I'm of course glad that I (and the lucky others on plane 1 were able to see the Grand Canyon, I'm also a little skeptical of Westwind's judgment to 1) fly us in such bad conditions and 2) fly half of our group on a plane that seems incredibly unsafe and with a pilot who apparently doesn't have basic communication skills. That's not just "bad conditions," that is bad judgement and completely unacceptable and infuriating when lifes are on the line. And finally, it's really disappointing that a once in a lifetime experience was turned into a harrowing, sickening flight from hell.

Review Text:
Westwind flew us from Phoenix to the Grand Canyon in a single-engine cessna, where we spent 30 minutes flying back and forth across the canyon before setting down at the local airport. From there, a van brought us to the canyon (10 minute ride), where we hiked down into the canyon with our guide. Finally, we had a provided box lunch on the canyon rim before flying back. In all, it was a magical experience. The plane was comfortable (noise-cancelling headphones provided), and offered a great view for everyone. Our guide was super friendly and extremely well qualified (how often do you get a geology grad student to give you a tour of the canyon).

Other tips: You can't hike from the top to the bottom of the canyon- I recall you get about 2 hours of hiking, and a full down/up hike would take over a day for an experienced hiker. Just hike until you're either tired or the guide suggests it's time to head back. The path itself serpentines down along the wall of the canyon, and has incredible views at every point. It has some steep drop-offs at the edges, but general it's around 10 feet wide and very safe. It might not be the best option for people afraid of heights, although my wife falls into that category, and while she was nervous she still made it down. We saw lots of people with kids, hikers with toddlers strapped into backpacks, and even some joggers! You should be in reasonably good physical shape though, and remember to save some stamina for the hike back up.

Review Text: If you're looking for a great way to experience the Grand Canyon but you only have a day...and you're not really within driving distance...and you don't mind paying for what you get, then this is for you. We were staying at the Boulders Spa and our adventure started with shuttle to a local airport followed by an awesome 75 minute flight in a 9 passenger, single turbo prop plane to the West Rim. Next up, a helicopter flight dropping off the rim down to the Colorado river where we boarded a pontoon boat for a powered ride upstream followed by a drift back to the dock. Helicopter back up, followed by lunch in a wild-west style town. Lunch was good and the town's a little silly but fine for an hour. A bus then took us to Skywalk which is at once, terrifying, awesome and anticlimactic. Be prepared to pay for pictures as they do not allow personal cameras out on the glass bridge. As a stand alone feature, it is okay, but as a part of the day it's perfect. Another bus ride to Guano Rock, which is breathtaking and another fabulous opportunity for pictures (you'll be doing this all day anyway). Back to the plane and back to Phoenix. If you get the chance to sit co-pilot, absolutely do. Our pilot and tour guide for the day, I'm embarrassed to say I'm not certain his name was Jim, was a fountain of knowledge about the area and just a genuinely nice guy. Just ask for the pilot who lived in Alaska and used to fly reconnaissance for the police and fire department in the greater Phoenix area. I would go out of my way to request him again. Total time was around 10 hours. As I mentioned up front, the trip's not cheap but worth every penny. All of the staff at Westwind were personable, professional and helpful.

Review Text: We took the Grand Canyon Skywalk Adventure Tour-West Rim and cannot say enough good things about Westwind Air and their staff.  The tour is exactly as described. Review Title: Page AZ departure for lake Powell and Grand Canyon
Review Text:
We booked by phone and boarded at Page airport while visiting lake Powell. We did not want to drive all the way to the Grand Canyon so we flew a scenic tour. Well worth it! At first the price thru me off, seemed steep at $270 a person for a 1.5 hour tour but it was 2 hours and included the canyon and Lake Powell flyover.

The views of the canyon were amazing and the time saved from driving was worth every penny. The first 20 minutes of flight are getting to the canyon, but it was worth the wait. The Grand Canyon tour does not claim to include lake Powell but we spent as much time over the lake as we did over the GC and it was as impressive maybe better.

Highly recommend this company and this tour. There is a longer one that also includes monument valley that may be worth consideration. They do not fly every hour every day so look at weather and book according. We were in the executive plane, nice captains chairs that hold 9 passengers and only good seats. The best seats are the row righ in front of the back bench. Most legroom and best window placement and size. Next best is right behind the pilot. Worst seats are still good, but the small windows offset form the seats make it hard to do uninterrupted video. Make sure to clean the window before you shoot or you get ugly smudge on the video. Also, take time to watch the view live, put the camera down once in a while.

About 10 minutes before we landed at Grand Canyon (50 minutes into the flight) I got motion sickness. I felt pretty sick when we landed and it was clear that I would not be able to take the jeep tour to the viewpoints. I was so disappointed. I have set foot on the West entrance of the Canyon before but this was my husbands first time. He stayed at the airport with me. I sat in the airport hoping to get better for the flight home and I did start feeling better. The Captain, Bruce Grubbs, came to me and asked if I felt well enough to take a short ride to Yavapai viewpoint which I did. He drove my husband and I into the park. Captain Grubbs happens to be a professional photographer and writer of many travel guides including the Grand Canyon. He was the best!! He SAVED our vacation and we will NEVER forget him. It was amazing to see it by air but it's a whole different experience on the ground. We are still trying to process the beauty and magnitude of this natural wonder. We would not have had this experience without him. Thank you Captain Grubbs.

We then went back to the airport and flew back to Phoenix. This flight took about 1 hour.

Our pilot Randy was amazing. Very experienced and knowledgable about the area. Great to get his insight as a local. Made me feel comfortable considering I was not sure about doing this type of plane ride. He was also great with the kids and took them for ice cream after lunch, nice touch.

Review Text: My husband and I chose this tour to view the Grand Canyon for the aerial view, and to reduce driving time. The flight and aerial view were spectacular! We had headsets on the plane portion  trip which dictated a  RECORDED  history  of the canyon and points of interest on our way there.  After this, I would have to say I was disappointed in the land portion of the tour. This part was supposed to be approximately three hours on land. We had exactly 55 minutes on land.  The brochure indicated that we would be making several stops at the most  scenic views of the canyon. However, there were only two stops for viewing.  Those parts of the tour were self-guided. It would have been better to have an experienced tour guide pointing out specific areas interest. We had a lunch in a cafeteria instead of the box lunch on the rim as advertised. The lunch took up 45 minutes of the ground time. The rest of the time was spent in a van to the Canyon and then back to the airport. While our tour guide in the van was exceptionally nice, I don't believe he was adequately trained to be a tour guide in regards to the Canyon  history itself.  We felt hurried on the ground tour and was told that they had a sunset plane tour and needed to get us back to pick up those other people. My thoughts are that you should focus on the customers that you have at the present time and not talk about future customers when you're with those people.  Instead of 5.5 hours for the tour as stated in the brochure, the tour instead from wheels up to wheels down was 4 3/4 hours long. These comments are meant to help improve the tour experience for future guests.

Review Title: Most amazing thing I have ever done in my life...
Review Text:
I know there are a lot of different options and packages available. We did the one where it was a plane ride to the top of the grand canyon, a helicopter ride down to the bottom and then a boat ride down the Colorado river.

Everything about this was well put together. They had someone pick us up at our resort and bring us to their hangar. They had free water, coffee and snacks available. We boarded a small Cessna plane and took about an hour and fifteen minute flight to the Grand Canyon. The view is breathtaking as some of the flight is over the GC. Our pilot got off the plane with us and guided us the rest of the day. He took us to the helicopter place and we jumped on a chopper that took us down to the bottom of the canyon. I cannot describe how magnificent the Grand Canyon is and you can't beat viewing it from a helicopter.

Once we were at the base of the Canyon, we boarded a pontoon boat and made about a half mile ride down the Colorado River and then floated back to where we started. We then took the helicopter back "up top" and hopped on a bus that took us to the SkyWalk. Our original pilot from the plane was always there to point us to our next stop or tell us to meet back somewhere at a particular time.

The SkyWalk was awesome and a little freaky. It's an engineering marvel and yeah it's a little scary. There were a couple of drama queens out there just freaking out. One little thing to note about the SkyWalk, they don't let you take your phone or camera out there so you have to buy their pictures. They have camera guys out there that will take your picture, and you can chose what pics you want to buy for a horrendous price (you are not obligated to buy anything). The problem was they were short staffed on camera guys and the ones that were there had some attitude problems. I didn't buy any pictures out of spite. You can get just as good of pictures from the area right next to the SkyWalk.

Next they took us to Guano Cafe to eat lunch. Our guide said it best that it was more like a metal building that served food than a cafe. The food was not good, seemed like a freezer meal that was only half way warmed up. I think they would've been better off telling you to just pack your own lunch or eat at some of the concession stands at the SkyWalk. However, there were a bunch of tables outside and you got to eat lunch overlooking the Grand Canyon which was pretty cool.

Guano Cafe was located at Guano Point. There's a lot of room to walk around and see the Canyon from a bunch of different places here. You can climb to the top of Guano Point and see a great 360 view. If you didn't already know, Guano is bat feces. This place is called that because there used to be a mining operation from this location that would mine bat droppings out of caves across the canyon. Apparently, it is a rich fertilizer and used in a lot of consumer products like makeup, etc. Anyway, you can see the old abandoned mining equipment and just marvel at the Canyon some more.

We headed back to plane and had a narrated flight back (about 1.5 hours). Although, I don't believe it to be the fault of the pilot, I would be remiss not to mention that the flight back was really, really turbulent (the flight there was not). My wife got sick and there were no vomit bags. Luckily, we had some coffee cups still in there from the morning that she used. I recommend taking some motion sickness meds before the flight back if you are affected by this type of thing as based on other reviews, this is common for the flight back.

In summary, this was a great trip and I would highly recommend it. Everything from the Skywalk tickets to meal vouchers were included in the total price ($1,300 for two). We will be going back and taking my parents at some point because this is really bucket list material.

Review Title: Excellent Grand Canyon Day Trip from Phoenix
Review Text:
Even though I graduated from Arizona State University and lived in Phoenix for several years, I had never visited the Grand Canyon. Shocking oversight, I know. So on my vacation to Phoenix, I decided to correct this by making a day trip with Westwind Air Service. They are based at Deer Valley Airport in north Phoenix, and their aircraft only seat a few folks, so you won't be part of a huge crowd.

If you are not a morning person, you may struggle to make departure time: they ask that you be at the airport by 7:30 AM for check-in for your flight. But trust me, its worth it. After a briefing about the journey you're about to take, you are escorted to the plane, and departure happens immediately. An audio program provides you with interesting facts about the history of areas you are flying over, as you proceed over the desert through scenic vistas, rolling valleys and plateaus, and past nearby mountains. My trip also included a stop at the Sedona airport to pick up a few more passengers, and Sedona has a fascinating air field atop a mesa.

Within ten minutes of landing in Sedona, we were airborne once again, this time heading for the Grand Canyon itself. The Grand Canyon Signature Tour, which was what I took, will actually take you over the south rim, and you will be treated to some truly spectacular views of one of the seven natural wonders of the world. Turn after turn, the awesome spectacle impresses you with its astonishing scale. If you can look at it, and not be stunned, that says far more about you than it says about the Grand Canyon or Westwind Air. There is no better way to take in the Grand Canyon than by air, and Westwind has perfected that experience.

But the tour doesn't there. Upon landing at the Grand Canyon airfield, you are met by Westwind's partners on this trip, Pink Jeep Tours. What follows is great half day expedition into the Grand Canyon park, a box lunch, a short hike through park itself with more spectacular vistas, and concludes with an IMAX theater experience about the history of the park itself. Then its back to the airport for your return journey to Phoenix.

Yes, the tour is not cheap. But if your staying in Phoenix and want to make a side trip to the Grand Canyon, bear in mind that driving up there will take the better part of four hours. Westwind can give you a full day of stunning vistas, and you'll back in Phoenix in time for dinner. So I consider it great value, and can't recommend it highly enough.

Review Title: Grand Canyon West Rim Skywalk Adventure Tour
Review Text:
Had a relatively short trip to Sedona for Spring Break with family and wanted to be able to see the Grand Canyon without doing a great deal of driving. This tour offered by Westwind Air Service was exactly what we were looking for.

The tour from Sedona departs from the Sedona airport nestled atop a small butte just south of town. A Cessna took my family and another family (9 passengers total---5 children 12 and under) on a narrated 75 minute flight to the Grand Canyon West airport. The views from the air of Sedona, Flagstaff, and the approach to the Grand Canyon were amazing---details you would miss in a larger plane or ground travel. Once at Grand Canyon West, we checked in for a helicopter ride into the canyon from Sundance Helicopters. The chopper takes you across the West Rim of the Canyon and down to a small landing area near the Colorado River. From there, you will board a pontoon boat to ride around on the Colorado for about 15-20 minutes before returning to the helicopter landing area. The helicopters operate like a shuttle service bringing parties into the canyon and taking groups out, running on a fairly perpetual basis. Once back at Grand Canyon West airport, we boarded a bus and traveled to the Hualapai Skywalk and then on to Guano Point where we had lunch which was included in our tour package.

The timing was pretty open-ended and we never felt rushed at all. Our pilot was very professional and knowledgeable. We felt safe the entire tour and felt that we really got our $ worth! Would definitely recommend for those wishing to see the Grand Canyon who do not mind spending a little more money to get there quickly and with views unmatched by any other means.

The Cessna took us up to the rim area in just over an hour and the approach to the Grand Canyon is truly spectacular. After landing we did the helicopter ride to the floor of the canyon. This was by far what we enjoyed the most. The boat ride is quite short but dipping toes in the Colorado and looking up the canyon walls makes this enjoyable. The Skywalk is the most commercial part of the West Rim and we felt photographed as if part of a wedding group but you could easily say no thanks after a few photos or opt out all together (no personal cameras allowed). The photo price is steep ($60 per photo or $80 for USB), however; I will treasure the excellent photo I purchased of my son and I. Guano Point is the last stop for a lunch that we thought was decent and the scenery is beautiful. To do the Grand Canyon justice you need more than a day but if you only have the day from Phoenix - this is the way to go. The staff of Westwind was first rate. We loved traveling in a small group. Lastly if you can go off season (before the end of April) you find great weather at the West Rim and no crowds!

Review Text:
I searched the internet for a company that did a South Rim tour of the Grand Canyon.

I was looking for a tour that:
• did the fly over as well as on a portion on the ground
• had newer aircraft
• had lots of window seats
• had consistently good tour reviews
Westwind had all of this. We arrived at the Deer Valley airport location ½ hour prior to the tour start time as directed. As we didn’t rent a car it was a $70 cab ride from Old Town Scottsdale where we stayed. We found out later that they do in fact pick you up, but this option wasn’t mentioned on booking.

There were 8 of us in the tour group and everyone had a window seat and earphones that played a pre-recorded commentary on what we were flying over. I found it interesting, as was the different landscapes we flew over on the way to the Grand Canyon (dry desert, pine forest, gentle hills, craggy monolithic rocks). And then we saw the Grand Canyon! WOW!!! What an amazing thing to experience....going from flat landscape to suddenly dropping off into cliffs of layered colour. I believe we flew over different portions of it for about 1/2hr before landing at a small airfield. Our pilot then turned into van driver and took us to 3 different locations where we could walk around outside by the edge (I stuck to the railing.....I did see some that were on the edge!!). The first spot was very cold and windy and had an information center with shop, we then carried on to the 2nd stop that housed the oldest resort NAME??? on the South Rim. There was a shop inside of it as well as one outside in another building (this one was full of art, books, trinkets etc). Our final stop was for lunch which was a good variety of cafeteria style food. Our pilot/guide was friendly and I think everyone felt comfortable and safe 
Additional:
• onsite office is bright, clean, has complimentary newspapers, snacks & beverages offered, I took extra time in the ladies washroom looking at all the stuff they had: mouthwash, hair care products, lotions & potions (a little more “fun” than the usual public restroom haha), large outdoor fountain
• EVERYONE that worked there was amazingly nice and I feel horrid I can't remember a single name!!
• After the tour we asked the office if there was a shuttle we could catch back to Old Town Scottsdale (or at least closer in so we didn’t have to pay a large cab fee again). We were put onto the company shuttle and the driver apologized for not picking us up that morning as she wasn’t aware of us. She gave us front door service and was a very friendly and informative lady (sorry, I can’t remember your name).
Maybe this service should be put out there a bit more visibly...unless we slipped thru the cracks the one time.

Do I recommend this company and this particular tour? Yes. Did I enjoy myself? Yes! A flight over the Grand Canyon was on my Bucket List so it was important to find the right tour company—and I did.

Tip: wear layers as it was very windy and cold at the first viewpoint we stopped at. Not so bad at any of the others.

Review Title: A wonderful addition to a great trip
Review Text:
I recently planned a very last-minute trip to the Grand Canyon and decided to include a Rim to Rim view flight. I called Westwind Air Service in the Phoenix area and scheduled a flight with Terry, who was most helpful and informative.

Due to a severe wind advisory at the Canyon for my scheduled flight day I decided to reschedule and once again spoke with Terry, who promptly moved my flight back one day.

On Wednesday 4/17 I drove to Grand Canyon Airport in Tusayan (a short drive from my hotel) and met with Jason, a very courteous employee who works at the counter checking passengers in for their flights.

Our pilot Brad (who has a great sense of humor) took us out to the Cessna 207 aircraft and as there were only three passengers, two people sat in the back and I sat up front. There was still some wind and we encountered a little bumpiness on the way to the canyon, but this was the bumpiest part of the flight.

Due to the interesting weather day there were cloud formations low over the canyon which provided additional striking views, and I found myself watching the sky as much as the canyon itself. I enjoyed the recording that played over headsets along the way, and also enjoyed talking with the pilot prior to and briefly following the flight.

Note: In the front seat you will not have an unobstructed view out of the side window as there is a wing strut that comes down and attaches to the body of the plane. However, you can see everything beneath you and if you bring your camera you can zoom past this for photos.

My goal was to see the grand canyon at different times of day and night and from different vantage points; flying over the canyon certainly helped fulfill that goal and added to the overall enjoyment of my trip.

I definitely recommend Westwind Air Service for anyone looking to take a view flight over the Grand Canyon.

Review Title: Excellent experience from Scottsdale to GC however
Review Text:
Really my only complaint was watching no one tip the pilot of WW, who is essentially your tour guide all day. At least our guy offered a LOT of information and background along the way, was able to get us in an out of lines faster etc. I understand that some countries are non tipping countries but I think that spelling it out at the desk at WW would be helpful. If you feel like it wasn't worth it then by all means let them know but a gratuity line item wouldn't be at all out of line IMO. You have the opportunity to buy your photo in front of the plane as the last thing you do at WW, perhaps when you are paying there could be a "would you like to add an additional gratuity to the pilot of your plane?" type question?

Actual Tour - I don't like cessnas but this was a larger one. Flight there was fine and very little turbulence. Flight back was very bumpy and while I wasn't nauseous, I was uneasy! The canned audio on the way in was slow but informative. A little too long IMO but I"m sure others found it very informational. I preferred the pilot's own views and sight information. The best thing is that the headphones drown out the plane's noise.

GC - Hopped out of plane, got in line for helicopter. Heli ride is very organized and professional and feels "safe." Short drop into the canyon. Steep rocky hike down (5 minutes) to the base where you hop on the pontoon boat. If you have knee or mobility problems then that little walk down will pose a bit of a problem. Plenty of older people being assisted as it's steeper grade and not even footing. Reasonably fit people should just watch their step and ankles! Great photo ops though if you turn around because the GC forms the base wall going up and the helicopters are flying back up to pick up more people.

Pontoon - short ride but fun. it was warmer here at the bottom than the windy top so it was nice to get out of the wind and have a short ride and relax. Beautiful and makes you want it to last a lot longer. No you do not get wet so no worries there...although we heard that occasionally people will jump in for no apparent reason! Out of the boat back at the dock and back up the rocky steps. Time to take some photos till you wait for your helicopter to pick you back up.

Back to the top where you get in line for Skywalk. If you don't know what this is, google it. I have a fear of heights and was cautiously fine. I also did not look down right away and did a lot of deep breathing. it's pretty scary! You can't take cell phones or cameras there but they have photogs of course so you can buy the pics after. Those range from 30 bucks i think to 120 maybe? that gets you your pics on a flash drive to do with what you please when you get home although they print off 4 for your right there, which i think is smart just in case your drive doesn't work later!! at least you have those 4 prints! You end up in the gift shop there until you leave.

Time for picnic style lunch - bbq chicken, cole slaw, brownies, corn, mashed potato and gravy. That type food. Looked fine to me...not sure what people complain about. It's included in the price. I have dietary restrictions so I didn't eat it but it looked fresh and tasty and everyone in my group finished their plates. Watch out for those pesky oversized ravens!! OH and plenty of opportunities for bathroom stops all day so in hindsight I would have drank a lot more water! There is time for a short hike after lunch and then some pics near the edge. Back on plane and back to phoenix.

All in all a very enjoyable trip and very well organized. Would do another trip with WW in a heartbeat and i faced my dislikes of small planes, helicopters and heights, all in one shot! if i can do it, so can you!

Review Text: I went with my grown daughter (no appropriate option above to choose from) to do the west grand canyon, sky walk 7.5 hour experience. This operation is 5* from beginning to end. Our trip was confirmed the day before. As instructed, we met Chick (in a white Nissan) outside our hotel lobby and were taken to the airfield where we met our pilot Chris. My daughter and I were the only passengers today.  Chris informed us that the grand canyon tour catered to the Asians and not to think him rude if he "bullied" his way through the throngs of people. We were informed that busloads of Asians are brought here daily from Las Vegas and that they push and do not understand the concept of waiting in line. True to his word, the place was mostly Asian (95+%) all pushing and moving in herds. It was so bad, that trying to exit the stall in the bathroom was almost impossible! Once outside of the restroom, Chris and another pilot arranged for the 2 groups to go ahead of the masses. We did our helicopter ride and pontoon boat down the Colorado river, then another helicopter ride back to the starting point. From there, we met up with Chris who whisked us off to a bus to do the skywalk. Very impressive, but expect long lines. Afterwards, we went to Guano Point for lunch. Be prepared to wait in line and be pushed and jostled. The food, I must admit, was poor at best- overcooked beans, corn, and then either pulled pork or bland chicken. There was also Cole slaw, mashed potatoes, a roll and chocolate cake, plus a bottle of water. My advice, pass on lunch or better yet, bring your own. I realize I went to see the sights and they were great... Lunch is just part of the package. After lunch, Chris took us on a hike and showed us the remains of the guano mining and lots of neat trivia. After this, back on the bus to a gift shop ( what else) and then back to the plane for the 1.5 hour return flight. This is a class operation and the experience would not have been as wonderful without a caring, knowledgeable pilot/ guide. I highly recommend this trip.

Pilot Jeff was amazing, answered all our questions, was patient,  funny, etc. Then we went to another viewpoint and you can also go on a small hike there if you want, then we headed back to Phoenix. The trip is a bit pricey, but totally worth it, hands down.

Review Title: Fantastic trip, if you have a free day well worth going!
Review Text:
Travelled with Westwind early February as part of 60th birthday treat whilst staying at Four Seasons, Scottsdale.
Early pick up from hotel, travelled to airport picking p 2 more passengers so just 4 of s on trip.
Pilot Jeff flew 90 minutes in Cessna to Grand Canyon, spectacular views as you near the Grand Canyon. Into helicopter on landing to be taken down to river for boat trip. We were really lucky as just the 4 of us on big boat with 'skipper' Nate who was very informative about the surrounding area.
Back up onto rim in helicopter and then onto Skywalk which was truly amazing! Just the 4 of us on as the coaches had not yet arrived, although I understand that it can get very busy in the high season.
Lunch on the rim of the canyon and then flight back to Phoenix.
Lots of opportunity for photos and Jeff took plenty for us to savour when we got home.
Cannot praise this company more, very professional and the tour was a delight, please try if you ave a free day, you will not be disappointed!

Review Text: The two of us thought our flight was smooth and love the fact your 1000 ft of the ground so visibility was excellent throught the terain and spoiled as I was in the front seat however everyone had their own window seat better that a helicopter 1 hour flight plus 25 min through south rim in canyon then land at the canyon airport then a 10 min ride into the park . Review Text:
Went to Grand Canyon and all was on time, friendly and helpful. Mike, our pilot and guide did an admirable job at both; personable, but not too intrusive. It is the kind of thing where you want the pilot concentrating on flying the plane and not jabbering too much. Costly, but worth it as it was a memorable family day.

The boat ride on the Colorado River was too short (they take you upstream and you float back to the dock in 20 mins), but that is no fault of Westwind.

Review Text:
Not a cheap day trip, but if you do not have the time for an overnight visit, or don't want to pack everything into a 14 hour day, this is the perfect alternative. You arrive at their airstrip and depart before 8AM. They provide breakfast snacks and drinks to start your day, take a picture before you depart, and off you go.

Look to be well maintained planes, nine seater we had for a group of six plus pilot, every seat a window seat. It was cool but brilliantly clear on take off. You get a good perspective of the valley and the elevation changes as you make your way northward. Sedona and the Red Rock are an incredible formation. I was surprised by the amount of development at the Grand Canyon. The flyover gives you a perspective you won't get anywhere else.

Small airport at the GC, smooth landing, and a short van ride to the lookout points. Pictures do not do this place justice. Two or three vantage points, a nice lunch included in the package, and another stop for gift shopping and you're back to the airport for the ride home. You have an opportunity to buy the picture that was taken in the morning for $10.

Back to our rental in south Phoenix by 4 in the afternoon. A long day, but well worth it. I am glad we took this tour. Shout out to Jeff our pilot for an informative and smooth flight.

A quality outing in the greater Phoenix area.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: The Only Way to See the Grand Canyon!
Review Text:
We booked a 7 hour flight with Westwind Air Service to see the Grand Canyon, primarily as we were staying in Scottsdale and driving 4+ hours to get there wasn't an option - especially with two children! What a smart service - their Strapline "Every passenger gets a window seat" is accurate - the seat configuration in the small aircraft ( a Cessna Caravan) was such that the pilot plus all 9 pasengers all had a window seat - what you want on a scenic flight! The flight left from Deer Valley Airport and flew over the most magnificent desert terraine I have ever seen in my life. Tonto National Forest, Sedona, Navajo Indian Reservation (amongst others) to the Grand Canyon South Rim, for a 30 minute over flight. The flight was narrated providing insights into the history and geology of the region, but mainly the flight carried a group of 6 adults and 2 children who sat gaping mouthed and wide-eyed at the impossible to take in views below! The flight was incredibly smooth - allowing the 4 year old to snuggle up for a quick nap (albeit as we few over the Grand Canyon!!!!)
From Grand Canyon Airport we were driven by the pilot in a spacious, air-conditioned mini-bus to the park were we first ate lunch (included in the price) and then explored various points on the rim on foot!!!
Our guide was happy to provide plenty of information and even managed to show us an elk hiding in the park before making our way back to Grand Canyon Airport for a fast peaceful flight home! It was the RIGHT WAY to see this magnificent Wonder of the World! The pilot was warm, knowledgeable and clearly qualified, and the aeroplane was clean and in good condition! Everything ran on time and the entire expedition lasted approximately 6 and a half hours! The tour group was limited to 8 passengers - nice and small! We drove ourselves to Deer Valley Airport but the other passengers had used Westwind Air's pickup service. WHen our boys are a little older we will use this company again to take one of their flights into the Canyon for a hike!!!!! I was an Amazing Unforgettable experience!
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text:
I recently spent $400 on a 3 hours scenic flight over the Grand Canyon, Monument Valley and Lake Powell. While definitely scenic, I was suprised at how underwhelmed I was with the experience. The staff were certainly courteous and the slightly drab recorded audio informative, but the experience left me feeling that it was a little under valued for the price. The land tour in Monument Valley was probably the highlight, as you go to go around the massive forms that make this place so famous.... and the following day, I got to sit with my legs dangling into the Grand Canyon at sunrise ... and that was an ahhhhhh experience.

So this review is not specifically about failings in the Westwind experience, I just felt that the structures involved were best scene from ground level to accentuate the experience.

Review Title: Touring Flight to the Grand Canyon
Review Text:
Despite the fact that we've flown over the Grand Canyon many times on our way out to the West Coast, my wife and I never actually visited it. On a recent trip to Scottsdale, we had one extra day to do some sightseeing. We decided to take a one-day trip to the Grand Canyon. This review is not about the Grand Canyon per se as there is little bad you can say about this magnificent natural wonder of the world. But I did want to give kudos to the tour service that provided the flight. The name of the company was Westwind Air Service tours. This company specializes on flights to the Grand Canyon from Deer Valley Airport in Phoenix.

My wife and I have been on our fair share of tours over the years, but this one-day tour was very special. Like many tour companies, this one comes to your hotel early in the morning and takes you (and other passengers) to the airport for the flight to the Grand Canyon. The people are extremely friendly, courteous, and do not skimp on anything. The plane is roomy and the pilot/tour guide is well trained. If you are lucky like I was, you can even get to sit in the right hand side in the cockpit next to the pilot. Our tour guide, who also flew the plane of 8 people, was a history buff and very knowledgeable about the Grand Canyon and surroundings. Going out to the Canyon you fly over Sedona, which is breathtaking from the air; you also fly over Tonto National Forest, and the famous "painted desert." The commentary is worth the price alone, but the scenery from plane is outrageous. The trip includes lunch at a cafeteria at the Grand Canyon with no limits on how much you eat. This was a very generous tour and we had a great time. I heartily recommend it to anyone wanting to see the Grand Canyon in a day. The price for our trip, including lunch was $399/person.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: Best way to see the Canyon!
Review Text:
My husband and I went to Scottdale for business and we decided to splurge ($600.00pp) to go see the Grand Canyon. This is hands down the best way to go. The staff was very nice and pleasant and our pilot was very knowledgeable. He answered all our questions, despite not being an "official" tour guide. We took the tour to the West area of the Canyon, including the skywalk, a helicopter ride, and a short boating tour od the Colorado river. It is the experience of a lifetime.
I would recommend everyone to go to Guano point and climb the rock; the view is majestic. Nobody else did it in our tour and they definitely missed a wonderful view.
The only bad thing is the lunch the Hualapai's offer (native American tribe that owns that land); I wouldntserve that to my dog. It's horrible. But, everything else compensates.
I would do it again; with the same company, the same place or even to the Sedona area perhaps. Happy travels!!!
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: We took the Page to Monument Valley, with Ground Tour in October. It was a lovely sunny day. Started from Page airport, which is very small, easy to find, and very informal. There was only the two of us, and a nice old chap for the pilot, in a Cesna. All very informative and professional. Took us to see the sights - Lake Powell, Navaho Mountain, Horseshoe Bend, Rainbow Bridge. Flight took about 45 minutes. When we landed at Monument Valley we were met by our Navaho Guide and his 4X4 (no waiting around). Again there was only the two of us, which was fortunate, because it was a bit cool outside and normally everyone would be in open seats on the back, but because there wa only the two of us, we asked to sit in with the guide, which was worth it because he was able to talk to us, keep us informed, and answer our questions about the Navaho culture. The Monument Valley wasbeautiful as expected - took lots of photos. Then back to the plane and back to Page. The pilot was very accommodating, and agreed to take a shorter route back to ease my wife's air sickness. We were doing a driving tour from Garnd Canyon, to Lake Powell, to Bryce, then Zion and Vegas, so this was a good way to take in Monument Valley without a long and uninteresting drive.

Review Title: Grand Canyon West Rim Adventure Tour
Review Text: My wife, our grand daughter and I spent a glorious day with our pilot Mike and another couple on this tour.  I would highly recommend this tour and Westwind Air Service.  The professionalism, courtesy and over all polished feel of these people made this a stress free and very enjoyable day.    We weren't rushed and were escorted to or accompanied through every event.  Mike told us which side of the buses to sit on for the best photo ops and knew all the little tricks to getting through the crowds.   Can't say enough how great the whole experience was.  Do this ASAP!

Review Text:
I visited Scottsdale the week after Christmas and had the great pleasure to take two trips with Westwind Air Service. The first was the Grand Canyon West Rim Adventure Tour - this is the trip to take to get a focused tour of the Grand Canyon. The helicopter flight to the bottom of the canyon is very cool - don't be afraid if this is your first helicopter experience - it's worth the flight. The pontoon ride is also neat - floating smoothly through the Grand Canyon with great views for pictures.The other stops during the tour are all excellent and offer more great sites for photographs.
The second tour was the Grand Circle Tour - flying through the Red Rock formations of Sedona offers wonderful views, more great perspectives on the Grand Canyon, and then the highlight of Monument Valley. Though you've seen all of these places in pictures and on TV, nothing can compare with seeing these locations first hand.
All of the management and staff of this company provide friendly, first class service to their customers. The pilots were all very professional, and the planes very comfortable. Make this number one on your list of things to do when visiting Phoenix/Scottsdale.

Review Text:
We were visiting Scottsdale and decided to do the full day Grand Canyon Adventure,air and ground tour.This 7 hour excursion included, plane,helicopter flight, pontoon ride on the Colorado River and entrance to the Skywalk which was all incredible.Westwind are a very professional team from being collected at our hotel, briefed at the airport and then flown and escorted by the pilot,Mike. Mike was particularly knowledgeable and helpful throughout the excursion.
From the spectacular views during the plane journey,the helicopter ride to the base of the canyon, the short pontoon ride and finally the scary walk on the Skywalk it was superb.
